candidate.derivedAnswer: A. May be skew; in fact, they must be skew.
candidate.answerReason: The supporting lines lie in distinct parallel base planes, so they cannot intersect. Since they are also stipulated not to be parallel, they must be skew. The pictured edges AB and CG illustrate such a pair.

methods.label: Exclude intersection and parallelism
methods.explanation: The two edges lie in distinct parallel base planes, so their supporting lines cannot intersect, even when extended. The question also states that they are not parallel. If these lines were coplanar, they would therefore intersect, a contradiction. Edges that are not coplanar and are not parallel are skew lines. Thus the edges must be skew, so A is the only valid choice.
methods.levelReason: Uses spatial-line classification, parallel planes, and the elementary definition of coplanar parallel lines.
